# About this reference

Every sheet and column of the VeroMesh model workbook, the standard format in which an organization gives VeroMesh its model. How to fill it in and load it is in the **User Guide** ("Maintaining the model in the workbook"). This reference is generated from the schema VeroMesh validates against, so it always matches what VeroMesh accepts.

Conventions, on every sheet:

- **ID** is a short key, unique across the whole model: letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`. Other sheets refer to a row by its ID.
- **Required** columns must be filled on every row; the template shows them in dark blue.
- Several values in one cell are separated by `;`.
- A reference may point at a row on another sheet, in another workbook, or already in VeroMesh from another source.
- Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`; amounts are plain numbers in the currency stated.

# Organization sheets

The organization sheets record who does what: usually from HR and the operating model.

## Objectives

Outcomes the organization intends to achieve, in a cascade from the enterprise down, with their owners, priorities and the objectives they pull against.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the objective. |
| Definition |  | text | What achieving this objective means, in a sentence or two. |
| Measured by KPIs |  | ID of KPIs (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of KPIs that measure progress. |
| Owner role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that owns this (ownership always sits with a role, not a person). |
| Level |  | one of: `enterprise`, `function`, `capability`, `process` | enterprise, function, capability or process: where the objective sits in the cascade. |
| Parent objective |  | ID of Objectives | ID of the objective this one contributes to, one level up. Empty for an enterprise objective. |
| Priority |  | number | When objectives pull against each other, the lower number wins: 1 is the highest priority. Compare objectives with the same parent. |
| Supports objectives |  | ID of Objectives (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of other objectives that progress on this one helps. |
| Conflicts with objectives |  | ID of Objectives (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of objectives that progress on this one can set back (on-time payment against working capital). A conflict counts both ways. |

## KPIs

Measures of progress. Used to route impact to their owners, not as targets; with a health threshold, they also show whether a capability is degraded.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the KPI. |
| Definition |  | text | How the KPI is calculated, and what a good value looks like. |
| Unit |  | text | e.g. percent, days, USD |
| Owner role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that owns this (ownership always sits with a role, not a person). |
| Computed from data products |  | ID of Data products (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the data products the KPI is calculated from. |
| Health of capabilities |  | ID of Capabilities (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the capabilities whose health this KPI shows. |
| Health threshold |  | number | The value past which the capability counts as degraded, in the KPI's unit. |
| Better when |  | one of: `higher`, `lower` | higher: degraded below the threshold. lower: degraded above it. |
| Current value |  | number | The latest value, usually loaded from the metrics layer, in the KPI's unit. |
| Measured on |  | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | When the current value was measured (YYYY-MM-DD). |

## Capabilities

What the organization is able to do; the spine of the model.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the capability. |
| Definition |  | text | What the capability covers, in business terms. |
| Owner role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that owns this (ownership always sits with a role, not a person). |
| Serves objectives |  | ID of Objectives (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the objectives this capability contributes to. |
| Parent capability |  | ID of Capabilities | ID of the broader capability this one is part of. Empty for a top-level capability. |
| Realized by processes |  | ID of Processes (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the processes that carry out this capability. |
| Produces data products |  | ID of Data products (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the data products this capability creates and answers for. |
| Consumes data products |  | ID of Data products (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the data products this capability depends on. |

## Processes

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the process. |
| Owner role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that owns this (ownership always sits with a role, not a person). |

## Roles

Job roles or positions. Not access-control roles.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the role. |
| Definition |  | text | What the role is accountable for, as its job description would say it. |

## People

Only role-relevant facts. Anything else is rejected by the validation rules.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the person. |
| Employee ID |  | text | From HR; used to match the same person across systems. Personal: shown only to those who need it. |
| Email |  | text | Work email. Used to match the person to their sign-in. Personal: shown only to those who need it. |
| Roles filled |  | ID of Roles (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the roles the person holds today. |
| Reports to |  | ID of People | ID of the person's manager. Personal: shown only to those who need it. |
| Department |  | text | Department or supervisory organization code, from HR. Used for an authority's scope. |
| Cost centre |  | text | Cost centre code, from HR or finance. Used for an authority's scope. |

# Governance sheets

The governance sheets record who may decide what, and which AI uses are approved: usually from finance, risk and the AI board.

## Policies

Internal policies and external regulations.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the policy or regulation. |
| Type | yes | one of: `Policy`, `Regulation` | Policy (internal rule) or Regulation (external law). |
| Jurisdiction |  | text | For regulations, e.g. US, EU. |
| Owner role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that owns this (ownership always sits with a role, not a person). |
| Bounds |  | ID of Authorities or Actions or Data products or Systems (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of authorities, actions, data products or systems this constrains. |
| Link |  | text | URL of the policy text. |

## Actions

Types of consequential action, e.g. 'approve supplier invoice'.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the action. |
| Part of process |  | ID of Processes | ID of the process the action belongs to. |
| Affects |  | ID of KPIs or Capabilities (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of KPIs or capabilities this action can move. Rows on the Impacts sheet are added here automatically. |

## Impacts

Materiality thresholds per action and KPI or capability. Rows have no ID of their own: each belongs to the row it names.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Action | yes | ID of Actions | ID of the action that can move the KPI or capability. |
| Impact on | yes | ID of KPIs or Capabilities | ID of the KPI or capability the action can move. |
| Materiality threshold | yes | number | Below this, the agent acts and informs the owner; above it, it consults the owner first. |
| Threshold unit | yes | text | e.g. USD per invoice, invoices per day. |

## Authorities

Grants to decide or act, with their limits.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the authority. |
| Holder | yes | ID of Roles or People or Agents | ID of the role, person or agent that holds this authority. |
| Actions covered | yes | ID of Actions (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the actions this authority lets the holder take. |
| Within capability |  | ID of Capabilities | ID of the capability the authority is limited to. Empty: wherever its actions apply. |
| Limit amount |  | number | The largest amount the holder may decide for one action, in the currency given. Empty: no amount limit. |
| Currency |  | text | ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD. |
| Limit kind |  | one of: `amount`, `percent`, `grade-steps`, `headcount` | amount (money, the default), percent (e.g. a raise), grade-steps (a promotion) or headcount (hires). |
| Limit value |  | number | For a limit kind other than amount: the largest value the holder may decide, e.g. 10 (percent). |
| Scope |  | one of: `any`, `reporting-line`, `department`, `cost-centre` | Over whom: any (default), reporting-line (people below the holder), department or cost-centre. |
| Scope unit |  | text | For department or cost-centre scope: the unit's code. Empty: the holder's own. |
| Valid from |  | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | First day the authority holds (YYYY-MM-DD). Empty: from now. |
| Valid until |  | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | Last day the authority holds (YYYY-MM-DD). Empty: until withdrawn. |
| Delegated by |  | ID of People or Roles or Policies | Who granted it: a person, a role, or the policy that establishes it. |
| Parent authority |  | ID of Authorities | For narrower copies (e.g. an agent's authority): the authority this is a bounded subset of. |

## Co-approvals

Further sign-offs: a second sign-off above an amount, or the steps of an approval chain. One row per tier or step. Rows have no ID of their own: each belongs to the row it names.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authority | yes | ID of Authorities | ID of the authority that requires this co-approval. |
| Approver role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role whose sign-off is needed. Give this or an approver relation. |
| Approver relation |  | one of: `manager`, `manager-of-manager`, `principal-manager` | Instead of a role: manager or manager-of-manager of the person the action is about, or principal-manager. |
| Step |  | number | Order in an approval chain (1, 2, ...): the decision lists its sign-offs in this order. Empty: first. |
| Above amount |  | number | Applies above this amount (or, for another limit kind, this value). Empty: always. |

## Agents

AI agents. Each acts for exactly one person.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the agent. |
| Acts for | yes | ID of People | ID of the one person the agent acts for. |
| Sign-in client ID |  | text | The client (application) ID the agent signs in with at your identity provider; links its sign-in to this agent. |
| Performs actions |  | ID of Actions (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the actions the agent is built to take. |
| Consumes data products |  | ID of Data products (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the data products the agent reads. |
| Runs on systems |  | ID of Systems (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the systems the agent works in. |

## AI use cases

Governance board decisions: which AI uses may run, for which agents and actions. From the board's register or minutes.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the approved AI use case. |
| Approved by | yes | ID of Roles | ID of the board or committee (as a role) that approved it, e.g. the AI review board. |
| Status | yes | one of: `approved`, `conditional`, `suspended`, `retired` | approved: may run. conditional: may run under the conditions given. suspended: must not run for now. retired: no longer in use. |
| Covers agents | yes | ID of Agents (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the agents this approval applies to. |
| Allows actions |  | ID of Actions (several, separated by `;`) | Actions the approved use may take. Empty: the approval does not limit actions. |
| Approved on |  | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | Date of the board's decision (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| Review by |  | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | When the board must review the approval again. |
| Conditions |  | text | Conditions the board attached. |

# Systems and data sheets

The systems and data sheets record where the work and its data live: usually from IT and the data office.

## Systems

Applications and platforms.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the system. |
| CMDB ID |  | text | The system's ID in your CMDB, so the two records can be matched. |
| Business owner |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role accountable for what the system is used for. |
| Technical owner |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role accountable for running and changing it. |
| Criticality |  | one of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` | How much the business depends on the system. |
| Lifecycle |  | one of: `planned`, `active`, `retiring`, `retired` | Where the system is in its life. |
| Sensitivity |  | one of: `Public`, `Internal`, `Confidential`, `Restricted` | The highest sensitivity of the data the system holds. |
| Regulatory scope |  | ID of Policies (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of regulations that apply. |

## Data products

Governed, owned data with known producers and consumers.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the data product. |
| Owner role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that owns this (ownership always sits with a role, not a person). |
| Steward role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that looks after the product's quality and definitions day to day. |
| Runs on systems |  | ID of Systems (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the systems the data product is stored in or served from. |
| Feeds data products |  | ID of Data products (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the data products built from this one (downstream). |
| Contains data elements |  | ID of Data elements (several, separated by `;`) | IDs of the business data elements the product holds. |
| Sensitivity |  | one of: `Public`, `Internal`, `Confidential`, `Restricted` | The highest sensitivity of the data it holds; it decides who may see it. |
| Catalog URN |  | text | The data product's URN in DataHub, if registered. |

## Data elements

Business-level data items. Physical columns in DataHub are bound to these.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ID | yes | ID | Unique key for this row (see the conventions above). |
| Name | yes | text | Display name of the data element. |
| Definition |  | text | What the data element means in business terms, as your glossary states it. |
| Critical |  | one of: `yes`, `no` | yes or no. Critical elements need an owner, steward and authoritative source. |
| Owner role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that owns this (ownership always sits with a role, not a person). |
| Steward role |  | ID of Roles | ID of the role that maintains its definition and quality day to day. |
| Authoritative source |  | ID of Systems | ID of the system that is the source of truth for it. |
| Sensitivity |  | one of: `Public`, `Internal`, `Confidential`, `Restricted` | How sensitive the data element is; it decides who may see it. |
| Data categories |  | one of: `Personal data`, `Health data`, `Payment card data`, `Financial reporting data` (several, separated by `;`) | Regulatory categories it falls into. |
| Retention |  | duration (ISO 8601, e.g. P7Y) | ISO 8601 duration, e.g. P7Y for seven years. |
| Catalog terms |  | text (several, separated by `;`) | DataHub glossary term or tag URNs that mark this element's columns; columns carrying them are suggested as bindings. |

## Column bindings

Which physical columns in DataHub hold each business data element. One row per column. Rows have no ID of their own: each belongs to the row it names.

| Column | Required | Holds | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Data element | yes | ID of Data elements | ID of the data element the column holds. |
| Column | yes | text | DataHub column URN: urn:li:schemaField:(<dataset URN>,<field path>). |
